Teaching Objectives
This course enables the student to:
Understand the principles and methods of IT project management
Execute the different phases of an IT project, from design to closure
Acquire skills in planning, organising, monitoring, and controlling projects
Identify and manage risks related to IT projects
Use IT project management tools and techniques
Work in a team in a project management context
Prerequisites:
Software engineering, information systems.
Course Content (21h)
1. IT Project Management: Review
Definition and stakes of IT project management
IT project production processes: realisation, management, quality
Types of IT projects (software development, infrastructure, etc.)
Stakeholders involved in an IT project
Relationships between project management and information systems
Traditional methodologies (V-cycle)
Agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban)
2. Planning and Estimation
Scope and objective definition
Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
Scheduling (Gantt chart, PERT)
Resource estimation (time, budget, personnel, costs, COCOMO)
Planning tools (Microsoft Project, Asana, etc.)
3. Risk Management and Monitoring
Risk identification and analysis (SWOT matrix, Ishikawa diagram)
Probability and impact assessment
Progress monitoring, change management
Communication and reporting
Dashboards and KPIs
4. Resource Management
Identifying required resources
Resource allocation to tasks
Conflict and priority management
5. Quality Management
Defining quality criteria
Implementing quality control procedures
Verification and validation testing
6. Project Closure
Project closure documentation
Knowledge and skills transfer
Stakeholder satisfaction evaluation
Project review and lessons learned
Assessment
Final examination (in person): 60%
Continuous assessment (CC): 40% — tests, personal work
